summary: Revision 4 of the ShimuraData plan, under the maintainer instruction of 2026-10-17. The foundations of Shimura data are now stated by open TauCetiRoadmap pull requests: ShimuraVarieties §§P.1–P.5 (pure data, Hermitian components, the representation–Hodge dictionary, homogeneous variations, Borel embedding, reflex field, levels and the GL₂/Siegel/torus examples), PELModuli §§M0.12 and M5.4, ReductiveGroupsPartII §§RG2.0a.3 and RG2.5, AdelicAlgebraicGroups §§1.3–1.4 and 4.3, and ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces §§ALS.F.1 and ALS.0.1–0.2. The 74 nodes they own are superseded and mapped to their owners. The plan keeps 49 nodes these roadmaps do not state — the Hilbert point comparisons, the rational-weight criterion, Mumford–Tate groups and Hodge genericity, uniqueness of the domain complex structure, general variations of Hodge structure, the compact dual and its descent to the reflex field, Kostant representatives and integral Bruhat/Schubert geometry, preabelian type, the Hilbert data, the Siegel and genus-two coordinate dictionaries, adelic neatness and the corrected Iw₁ criterion — and adds four on the generality of data: the additional axioms SV2*, SV4–SV6, the SV5 criterion, PEL type with the PEL–Hodge–abelian–preabelian chain, and the lifting of connected data to data satisfying every axiom. All six layers are planned; a restructure proposal reverses the atlas edges to ShimuraVarieties and PELModuli and merges D0 into D5 and D2 into D3. Its independent review (REV-ShimuraData~4) corrected the Mumford–Tate ideal (the largest Hopf ideal in the kernel of h, not the kernel), the behaviour of SV2* under products, a unit computation and a sign in the lifting argument, rewrote the generic source matches, and added the reflex field of a product and the Borel-embedding comparison that consumers of superseded nodes need.

nodes.title: Real points of the Hilbert groups
nodes.statement: Let F be a totally real number field of degree d with real embeddings σ₁,…,σ_d, G=Res_{F/ℚ}GL₂ and G*=G×_{Res_{F/ℚ}G_m}G_m the fibre product of det:G→Res_{F/ℚ}G_m with the diagonal G_m→Res_{F/ℚ}G_m. The Weil-restriction point comparison gives G(ℝ)=GL₂(F⊗_ℚℝ), and the ℝ-algebra isomorphism F⊗_ℚℝ≅ℝ^d, x⊗r↦(σ_i(x)r)_i, identifies it with ∏_i GL₂(ℝ), sending a∈GL₂(F) to (σ₁(a),…,σ_d(a)). Under this identification G*(ℝ) is the set of tuples (g_i) whose determinants all equal one t∈ℝ^×, of either sign. Both identifications are isomorphisms of real Lie groups; G(ℝ) has 2^d connected components, indexed by the signs of the d determinants, and G*(ℝ) has exactly two.
proofSteps: RG2.0a gives G(ℝ)=GL₂(F⊗_ℚℝ), naturally in the coefficient algebra.
Because F is totally real, x⊗r↦(σ_i(x)r)_i is an ℝ-algebra isomorphism F⊗_ℚℝ≅ℝ^d (the archimedean case of AA §1.4's local factors); GL₂ of a finite product of rings is the product of the GL₂'s.
Points of a fibre product are the fibre product of the points, and the diagonal G_m(ℝ)→(Res_{F/ℚ}G_m)(ℝ)=(ℝ^×)^d is the scalar embedding, so G*(ℝ) consists of the tuples with a common determinant t.

GL₂(ℝ) has the two components det>0 and det<0, so G(ℝ) has 2^d. For a fixed sign of t, dividing every g_i by |t|^{1/2} and, when t<0, multiplying by one fixed element of determinant −1 identifies {(g_i): det g_i=t for all i} with ℝ_{>0}×∏_iSL₂(ℝ), which is connected; hence G*(ℝ) has two components.
ALS.F.1 applied to the closed embeddings G_ℝ⊂GL_{2d,ℝ} and G*_ℝ⊂G_ℝ makes the identifications isomorphisms of real Lie groups.

sources.match: For a quaternion algebra B over a totally real F, Milne tabulates B⊗_ℚℝ and G(ℝ) factor by factor over the real embeddings, with GL₂(ℝ) and the standard h at each split place; the split case B=M₂(F) is this node's G, and the common-determinant condition is the fibre product added here.

hypotheses: F is a totally real number field of degree d≥1; G and G* are as stated, with G* the fibre product over Res_{F/ℚ}G_m.

Weil restriction and its point comparison are ReductiveGroupsPartII §RG2.0a's (WeilRestriction.pointsMulEquiv); the archimedean local factor of restriction of scalars is AdelicAlgebraicGroups §1.4's; the Lie group structure on real points is ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces §ALS.F.1's (realPoints_lieGroup).
acceptance: For F=ℚ, G=G*=GL₂ and both identifications are the identity of GL₂(ℝ).
For F=ℚ(√2), G(ℝ)=GL₂(ℝ)×GL₂(ℝ) has four components; the pair (I₂,diag(1,−1)) lies in G(ℝ) but not in G*(ℝ), whose two components consist of the pairs with determinants of a common sign.
For F=ℚ(√2) the rational element diag(√2,1)∈GL₂(F) goes to (diag(√2,1),diag(−√2,1)), whose determinants have opposite signs; diag(√2,√2) goes to a pair with common determinant 2.

nodes.title: Finite-adelic points of the Hilbert groups
nodes.statement: For the same F, AdelicAlgebraicGroups §1.4 (restriction of scalars on adelic points) identifies G(𝔸_{ℚ,f})=GL₂(F⊗_ℚ𝔸_{ℚ,f}) with GL₂(𝔸_{F,f}) as topological groups, carrying the diagonal image of G(ℚ)=GL₂(F) to the diagonal image of GL₂(F), naturally in algebraic group maps. Under it G*(𝔸_{ℚ,f}) is the closed subgroup of g∈GL₂(𝔸_{F,f}) with det g in the image of 𝔸_{ℚ,f}^×→𝔸_{F,f}^×, and G*(ℚ) is the subgroup of GL₂(F) with determinant in ℚ^×. Every compact open subgroup of G*(𝔸_{ℚ,f}) is V∩G*(𝔸_{ℚ,f}) for some compact open subgroup V⊂GL₂(𝔸_{F,f}), and every such intersection is compact open in G*(𝔸_{ℚ,f}). Nothing is asserted about discreteness of G(ℚ) or G*(ℚ) in the finite adeles.
proofSteps: AA §1.4 gives the topological isomorphism together with its diagonal and naturality clauses.

Apply AA §1.3's functoriality to det:G→Res_{F/ℚ}G_m and to the diagonal G_m→Res_{F/ℚ}G_m; points of the fibre product are the fibre product of points, giving the determinant locus. It is closed because both maps are continuous and the ideles are Hausdorff.

Compact opens: given a compact open subgroup U of G*(𝔸_{ℚ,f}), pick a compact open subgroup V₀ of GL₂(𝔸_{F,f}) with V₀∩G*⊂U and normalized by U (intersect the finitely many U-conjugates of a small V₀, U being compact and open in G*); then V=UV₀ is a compact open subgroup with V∩G*=U(V₀∩G*)=U. Conversely V∩G* is open in G*, and compact because G* is closed.
No discreteness is claimed: G*(ℚ) contains the infinite group SL₂(O_F), which lies in the compact open GL₂(Ô_F)∩G*.

sources.locator: Example 5.24, pp.63–64; §5, compact open levels in G(𝔸_f), pp.57–58
sources.match: Milne's quaternion example gives the group G with G(ℚ)=B^×, which for B=M₂(F) is GL₂(F); the levels of the Shimura variety are compact open subgroups of G(𝔸_f). The base-change comparison and the determinant locus of G* are supplied by the adelic-groups roadmap and the fibre product, not by this page.

hypotheses: F, G and G* are as in D0/hilbert-real-points.
The adelic restriction-of-scalars isomorphism (base-change-adelic) is AdelicAlgebraicGroups §1.4's; functoriality of adelic points under the determinant and the diagonal is §1.3's.
acceptance: For F=ℚ both groups are GL₂ and the identification is the identity of GL₂(𝔸_{ℚ,f}).
For F=ℚ(√2), diag(√2,√2)∈GL₂(F) has determinant 2∈ℚ^× and lies in G*(ℚ); diag(√2,1) has determinant √2∉ℚ and lies in G(ℚ) but not in G*(ℚ).
For V=GL₂(Ô_F), V∩G*(𝔸_{ℚ,f}) is the group of integral matrices whose determinant lies in the image of Ẑ^×.

nodes.title: Rational weight criterion
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional rational V with an algebraic real S-action h, its weight w_h=h∘(inverse diagonal) descends to a ℚ-cocharacter of GL(V) if and only if the real weight decomposition is the scalar extension of an internal finite ℚ-grading. The rational grading acts by t^n on weight n. The full homomorphism h need not descend to ℚ.
proofSteps: A rational Gm-action has rational eigenspaces. Conversely a rational grading defines t↦tⁿ on its rational summands, whose real extension is h∘w.

sources.match: The passage says a rational Hodge structure corresponds to an S-action whose weight map is rational. R4 supplies the rational Gm eigenspace dictionary.

nodes.title: Mumford–Tate group
nodes.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional ℚ-vector space and h:S→GL(V)_ℝ an algebraic homomorphism with weight defined over ℚ (a rational Hodge structure, D1/rational-weight-criterion). Let K_h⊂O(GL(V)) be the kernel of the ℚ-algebra map O(GL(V))→O(GL(V))⊗_ℚℝ→O(S) given by h: the ideal of the ℚ-Zariski closure of h(S), which need not be a subgroup. Let I_MT be the largest Hopf ideal contained in K_h, the sum of all Hopf ideals contained in K_h. Then MT(V)=Spec(O(GL(V))/I_MT) is the smallest ℚ-algebraic subgroup of GL(V) whose real extension contains h(S): a Hopf ideal I satisfies h(S)⊂V(I)_ℝ exactly when I⊂K_h, exactly when I⊂I_MT. K_h is also the kernel of the complexified split map O(GL(V))→O(S_ℂ)=ℂ[z₁^{±1},z₂^{±1}]. The image of the weight cocharacter lies in MT(V) and is trivial in weight zero. MT uses the whole S-map, not its restriction to the norm-one circle.
proofSteps: h is a homomorphism of real algebraic groups, so h*:O(GL(V))⊗ℝ→O(S) respects comultiplication, counit and antipode; K_h is the kernel of its restriction to O(GL(V)), the ideal of the rational functions vanishing on h(S).

A sum of Hopf ideals is a Hopf ideal (Tau Ceti's HopfIdeal.sSup_toIdeal: the join of a set of Hopf ideals is a Hopf ideal whose ideal is the join of their ideals), so I_MT, the join of all Hopf ideals contained in K_h, is a Hopf ideal contained in K_h that contains every such Hopf ideal. K_h itself need not be one: h*⊗h* lands in O(S)⊗_ℝO(S), and the kernel of O(GL(V))⊗_ℚO(GL(V))→O(S)⊗_ℝO(S) can be larger than K_h⊗O+O⊗K_h (test mtKernelNotHopf).

Minimality: for a Hopf ideal I, h factors through V(I)_ℝ iff h* kills I⊗ℝ iff h* kills I (h* is ℝ-linear and I spans I⊗ℝ) iff I⊂K_h iff I⊂I_MT. nodes.title: Uniqueness of the domain complex structure
nodes.statement: Let (G,X) be a pure Shimura datum with the complex structure of ShimuraVarieties §P.2, for which §P.3 makes the Hodge filtration of every representation a holomorphic variation. That complex structure is the only one with this property: if J′ is a complex-manifold structure on the same underlying smooth manifold X for which, for one faithful real representation ρ of G, the filtration map x↦F_x(ρ) into the flag manifold of ρ is holomorphic, then the identity of X is a biholomorphism between J′ and the §P.2 structure. One faithful representation suffices because every representation is a subquotient of tensor constructions on ρ and its dual.
proofSteps: The filtration map of a faithful ρ is injective with injective differential (the Borel embedding of ShimuraVarieties §P.3), so it is an immersion of the smooth manifold X into the flag manifold.
If it is holomorphic both for J and for J′, its differential intertwines J and J′ with the complex structure of the flag manifold; injectivity of the differential forces J=J′ on every tangent space.

Two integrable complex structures with the same almost complex structure have the same local holomorphic functions, so the identity is biholomorphic. Tensor, dual and subquotient constructions transport holomorphicity from ρ to every representation, so the conditions 'for one faithful ρ' and 'for every representation' agree.

sources.match: Milne's Proposition 5.9 asserts that X has a unique complex-manifold structure for which every representation gives a holomorphic family of Hodge structures, and that each such family is then a variation; the proof reduces to one faithful representation. ShimuraVarieties §P.3 states the existence half; this node is the uniqueness half.

This is Hansen–Johansson's Definition 4.1: no central isogeny of derived groups is required, and no isomorphism of the full orbits.
proofSteps: Quantify over the Hodge-type witness and connected-adjoint datum isomorphism; descend the predicate from any chosen component.

sources.match: Hansen–Johansson §4.1 recall Hodge and abelian type and in Definition 4.1 call a connected datum preabelian when it is isomorphic to (G̃^ad,X̃⁺) for a Hodge-type datum (G̃,X̃), and a datum (G,X) preabelian when (G^der,X⁺) is; no central isogeny of derived groups is required.

nodes.title: PEL–Hodge–abelian–preabelian implications
nodes.statement: For every pure datum: PEL type (D4/pel-type) implies Hodge type, through PELModuli §M0.12's Siegel morphism; Hodge type implies abelian type, through the identity of the derived group; abelian type implies preabelian type, by forgetting the derived isogeny. These are implications between separately defined predicates; no converse is asserted. The restriction-of-scalars Hilbert datum over a real quadratic field is of abelian type but not of Hodge type, because it fails SV5 while Hodge-type data satisfy SV2* and hence SV5.
proofSteps: PEL⇒Hodge: the witness of D4/pel-type carries PELModuli §M0.12's siegelMorphism, a closed immersion of groups mapping the domain into the Siegel domain.
Hodge⇒abelian: take the Hodge-type datum itself and the identity of its derived group.
Abelian⇒preabelian: forget the central derived isogeny and keep the adjoint isomorphism.

Non-converse: a Hodge-type datum (G,X)⊂(GSp,ℋ^±) satisfies SV2* because Int(h(i)) is Cartan on GSp_ℝ/G_m and restricts to a Cartan involution of the closed subgroup G_ℝ/w(G_m); SV2* gives compactness of Z(ℝ)/w(ℝ^×) and so SV5 (D4/sv5-criterion). The Hilbert datum over ℚ(√2) fails SV5 (D4/additional-axioms test) but is of abelian type through the scalar-determinant datum.

nodes.title: Additional axioms SV2*, SV4, SV5, SV6
nodes.statement: For a pure Shimura datum (G,X) with weight w_X:G_{m,ℝ}→Z(G)°_ℝ and centre Z=Z(G), define four predicates. SV2*: for h∈X, Int(h(i)) is a Cartan involution of G_ℝ/w_X(G_m) (Deligne's 2.1.1.5). SV4: w_X is defined over ℚ, i.e. the weight is rational (Deligne's 2.1.1.4). SV5: Z(ℚ) is discrete in Z(𝔸_f). SV6: the torus Z° splits over a CM field. Each is a property of the datum: independent of h∈X and invariant under isomorphism of data. With SV1–SV3 of ShimuraVarieties §P.1, SV4 and SV2* are Deligne's conditions 2.1.1.1–2.1.1.5. SV2* implies SV2, and under SV4 every rational representation of G and every h∈X give a rational Hodge structure.
hypotheses: (G,X) is a pure Shimura datum in the sense of ShimuraVarieties §P.1 (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #933): G connected reductive over ℚ, X a nonempty full G(ℝ)-class of algebraic h:S→G_ℝ satisfying SV1–SV3, with S the Deligne torus of ReductiveGroupsPartII §RG2.0a.3.

Cartan involutions are ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces §ALS.0.1's (compact twisted real form, with the Killing criterion on the derived algebra and a separate condition on the central torus); Z(𝔸_f) carries AdelicAlgebraicGroups §1.3's topology; a CM field is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real number field (Mathlib NumberField.IsCMField).
proofSteps: Independence of h: points of X are G(ℝ)-conjugate; conjugation fixes the central weight and carries Int(h(i)) to Int(gh(i)g⁻¹), and inner automorphisms preserve Cartan involutions (ALS.0.1, conjugacy of Cartan involutions). SV4–SV6 do not involve h.
SV2*⇒SV2: by ALS.0.1's Killing criterion, a Cartan involution of G_ℝ/w_X(G_m) is positive on the derived algebra, which is the Lie algebra of G^ad_ℝ; that positivity is SV2.
Isomorphism invariance: an isomorphism of data is a ℚ-isomorphism of groups carrying X to X′, so it carries weights, centres and their ℚ-structures to each other.

SV4 and rational Hodge structures: if w_X is defined over ℚ then ρ∘w_X is a ℚ-cocharacter of GL(V) for every rational representation ρ, and D1/rational-weight-criterion makes (V,ρ∘h) a rational Hodge structure.

Products: the weight of (G₁×G₂,X₁×X₂) is (w₁,w₂) and its centre is Z₁×Z₂, so SV4 and SV5 hold for the product iff they hold for both factors, and so does SV6 because a compositum of CM fields is CM. G_i/w_i(G_m) is a quotient of (G₁×G₂)/(w₁,w₂)(G_m) and the image of a compact twisted form is compact, so SV2* passes from the product to each factor. The converse fails: (Z₁×Z₂)/(w₁,w₂)(G_m) can contain a split torus although each Z_i/w_i(G_m) is anisotropic (test additionalProductSV2Star).
acceptance: SV2* holds for one h∈X iff it holds for every h∈X.
SV2* implies SV2.
Under SV4 every rational representation and every h∈X give a rational Hodge structure.

Each of SV2*, SV4, SV5, SV6 is invariant under isomorphism of data. SV4, SV5 and SV6 hold for a product iff they hold for both factors; SV2* for a product implies SV2* for both factors, and not conversely.
The GL₂ datum satisfies SV2*, SV4, SV5 and SV6.

The quaternion datum of Milne's Example 5.24 with exactly one split real place of ℚ(√2) satisfies SV1–SV3 but not SV4.
The torus datum (G_m,{1}) with trivial h satisfies SV1–SV6 but not SV2*.

The product of two copies of the GL₂ datum satisfies SV4, SV5 and SV6, and each factor satisfies SV2*, but the product does not: its weight is r↦(r⁻¹I₂,r⁻¹I₂), and its centre G_m×G_m modulo that weight is a split G_m, on which Int h(i) is the identity while ℝ^× is not compact.

nodes.title: Discreteness criterion for the rational centre
nodes.statement: For a ℚ-torus T let T_a be its largest ℚ-anisotropic subtorus (the identity component of the common kernel of the ℚ-rational characters). Then T(ℚ) is discrete in T(𝔸_f) if and only if T_a(ℝ) is compact, that is, T_a stays anisotropic over ℝ. Consequently a pure datum (G,X) satisfies SV5 if and only if the largest ℚ-anisotropic subtorus of Z(G)° is anisotropic over ℝ.
hypotheses: T is a torus over ℚ; T(𝔸_f) carries AdelicAlgebraicGroups §1.3's topology and T(ℚ) its diagonal image.
For the consequence, (G,X) is a pure datum (ShimuraVarieties §P.1); Z(ℚ) is discrete iff Z°(ℚ) is, Z°(ℚ) having finite index.
proofSteps: AdelicAlgebraicGroups §1.3 (discreteness in the finite adeles alone): T(ℚ) is discrete in T(𝔸_f) iff T(ℚ)∩U is finite for one compact open U; for U the integral points of a model this intersection is an arithmetic subgroup T(ℤ).

Ono's theorem as used by Milne: T(ℤ)∩T_a(ℚ) has finite index in T(ℤ), and T_a(ℝ)/(T(ℤ)∩T_a(ℚ)) is compact. The compactness half is AdelicAlgebraicGroups §3.4 (arithmetic quotients of anisotropic groups are compact) applied to T_a; the finite-index half is requested.

For a faithful representation T⊂GL_n, T(ℤ)⊂GL_n(ℤ) is discrete in T(ℝ)⊂GL_n(ℝ), and so is T(ℤ)∩T_a(ℚ) in T_a(ℝ); a discrete subgroup with compact quotient of the abelian Lie group T_a(ℝ) is finite iff T_a(ℝ) is compact. With the finite-index statement, T(ℤ) is finite iff T_a(ℝ) is compact.
For a datum, apply this to T=Z(G)°.
acceptance: For G_m, T_a=1, so ℚ^× is discrete in 𝔸_f^×.
For the norm-one torus of ℚ(i), T_a=T has compact real points U(1), so T(ℚ) is discrete; T(ℤ)={±1,±i}.
For the norm-one torus of ℚ(√2), T_a=T has real points {(a,b):ab=1}, not compact, and T(ℤ)={±(3+2√2)^n}={±(1+√2)^{2n}} is infinite (1+√2 has norm −1; ShimuraData/E19), so T(ℚ) is not discrete.
The GL₂ datum satisfies SV5 and the restriction-of-scalars Hilbert datum over ℚ(√2) does not.

sources.match: Milne proves that T(ℚ) is discrete in T(𝔸_f) exactly when the largest ℚ-anisotropic subtorus has compact real points, using Ono's theorem on arithmetic subgroups of tori, checks G_m and the norm-one tori of ℚ(i) and ℚ(√2), and restates SV5 through the centre. Milne's list of the norm-one units of ℤ[√2] includes the odd powers of 1+√2, which have norm −1 (E19).

nodes.title: PEL type
nodes.statement: A pure datum (G,X) is of PEL type if it is isomorphic, as a datum, to RationalPELDatum.toShimuraDatum(𝒟) of PELModuli §M0.12 for a rational PEL datum 𝒟=(B,*,V,ψ,h) with V≠0 whose similitude group G_𝒟 is connected and satisfies SV3; the witness is 𝒟 together with the isomorphism. By §M0.12 the Siegel embedding G_𝒟→GSp(V,ψ) is a morphism to the genus-g Siegel datum (2g=dim_ℚV), so PEL type implies Hodge type; a datum of PEL type satisfies SV4.
hypotheses: Rational PEL data, their groups, domains and Shimura data are PELModuli §§M0.6–M0.12's; data and their isomorphisms are ShimuraVarieties §P.1's.
Connectedness of G_𝒟 and SV3 are imposed explicitly: §M0.12 shows that type D groups are disconnected and that wholly definite unitary data of rank at least two fail SV3 (see ShimuraData/E18).
proofSteps: The predicate is an existential over rational PEL data with V≠0, connected group and SV3, and over isomorphisms of data.
Invariance under isomorphism: compose the witness isomorphism.
PEL⇒Hodge: §M0.12's siegelMorphism is a closed immersion of groups carrying X_𝒟 into the Siegel domain, a Hodge-type witness in the sense of ShimuraVarieties §P.1.
SV4: the weight of toShimuraDatum(𝒟) acts on V by the scalar r⁻¹, which is defined over ℚ.
acceptance: PEL type is invariant under isomorphism of data.
PEL type implies Hodge type.
A datum of PEL type satisfies SV4.
A rational PEL datum with V≠0, connected group and SV3 gives a datum of PEL type.
The genus-g Siegel datum (g≥1) is of PEL type, through the Siegel PEL datum with B=ℚ (PELModuli §M5.1).
For totally real F the scalar-determinant Hilbert datum of PELModuli §M5.4 is of PEL type.
The quaternion datum of Milne's Example 5.24 with exactly one split real place of ℚ(√2) is not of PEL type, since it fails SV4.

nodes.title: Lifting connected data to full data
nodes.statement: Let H be a semisimple ℚ-group and h̄:S→H^ad_ℝ satisfy SV1–SV3 (a connected datum in ShimuraVarieties §P.1's convention). Then there are a connected reductive ℚ-group G with G^der=H and an algebraic h:S→G_ℝ with ad∘h=h̄ such that the G(ℝ)-class of h is a pure datum satisfying SV1, SV2, SV2*, SV3, SV4, SV5 and SV6. In Milne's two steps: first G with G^der=H, rational weight and centre split by a CM field; then, replacing G by the preimage of the smallest subtorus of G/G^der whose real points contain the image of h, SV2* as well.
hypotheses: H is semisimple over ℚ and h̄ satisfies SV1–SV3; the connected convention, special pairs and maximal tori through h̄ are ShimuraVarieties §§P.1 and P.5's.
The central extension with prescribed derived cover (Milne–Shih 1982, 3.1, as quoted by Milne 2013) is requested from ReductiveGroupsPartII §RG2.1.
proofSteps: Replace h̄ by an H^ad(ℝ)^+-conjugate factoring through T̄_ℝ for a maximal ℚ-torus T̄ of H^ad (Milne 2013, Proposition 8.1; ShimuraVarieties §P.5). T̄_ℝ is anisotropic by SV2, so complex conjugation acts as −1 on X*(T̄) and T̄ splits over a CM field L, chosen Galois over ℚ.
Take a central extension 1→N→G→H^ad→1 with G^der=H and N a product of copies of Res_{L/ℚ}G_m (ReductiveGroupsPartII §RG2.1, requested).

The preimage T of T̄ is a maximal torus. Lift μ_h̄ to μ∈X_*(T), possible because N is connected. Its weight w=−μ−ιμ lies in X_*(N); X_*(N) is an induced Gal(ℂ/ℝ)-module, so its Tate group Ĥ⁰ vanishes and w=(ι+1)μ₀ with μ₀∈X_*(N). Replacing μ by μ+μ₀ gives weight −(1+ι)(μ+μ₀)=w−w=0, in particular rational (Milne writes μ−μ₀, which with w=−μ−ιμ doubles the weight: ShimuraData/E20); let h correspond to μ.

Replace G by the preimage of the smallest subtorus of G/G^der whose real points contain the image of h; it is ℝ-anisotropic, which gives SV2*. SV1 and SV3 depend only on h̄; SV2 follows from SV2*; SV5 follows from SV2* and D4/sv5-criterion, since Z(ℝ)/w(ℝ^×) is compact; SV6 holds because the new centre lies in N, split by L.
acceptance: For H=SL₂ and its connected datum on ℍ, G=GL₂ with its usual h is such a lift.
The fundamental PGL₂ cocharacter does not lift to SL₂ (ShimuraVarieties §P.1 Check), so a lift with G^der=SL₂ must have G≠SL₂.
For H trivial the construction returns a torus G and may return G=1 with h trivial.

nodes.title: Reflex field of a product datum
nodes.statement: For pure data (G₁,X₁) and (G₂,X₂) with product (G₁×G₂,X₁×X₂) (ShimuraVarieties §P.1), the reflex field of the product is the compositum inside ℚ̄: E(G₁×G₂,X₁×X₂)=E(G₁,X₁)·E(G₂,X₂). The same holds for finitely many factors.
hypotheses: (G₁,X₁) and (G₂,X₂) are pure Shimura data in the sense of ShimuraVarieties §P.1 (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #933); their product, with componentwise h, is §P.1's product datum.

Cocharacter classes and reflex fields are ShimuraVarieties §P.3's: E(D) is the fixed field of the open stabilizer in Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) of the conjugacy class of μ_h, and E(D′)⊂E(D) for every datum morphism D→D′.
proofSteps: For h=(h₁,h₂)∈X₁×X₂, μ_h=(μ_{h₁},μ_{h₂}), and two cocharacters of G₁×G₂ are conjugate iff their components are, so the class of the product is the pair of classes and σ∈Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) fixes it iff σ fixes both.
The stabilizer of the pair is the intersection of the two open stabilizers; by Galois theory its fixed field is the compositum of their fixed fields, E(G₁,X₁)E(G₂,X₂).

This refines §P.3's functoriality: the two projections are datum morphisms, so each E(G_i,X_i) lies in the reflex field of the product; the stabilizer computation gives equality. Induct on the number of factors.
acceptance: The product of two Siegel data has reflex field ℚ.
For an imaginary quadratic field K, the product of the GL₂ datum with the torus datum of the CM type of an elliptic curve with CM by K (reflex field K) has reflex field K.
For CM types (E₁,Φ₁) and (E₂,Φ₂) with reflex fields E₁* and E₂*, the product of their torus data has reflex field E₁*E₂*, not E₁*∩E₂*.
The product with the one-point datum of the trivial group has the reflex field of the other factor.

sources.match: Milne shows that the conjugacy class of μ_x is defined over ℚ̄ (Lemma 12.1), defines E(G,X) as the fixed field of its Galois stabilizer (Definition 12.2) and notes that an inclusion of data reverses the inclusion of reflex fields (Remark 12.3(c)); the product formula is derived here from the definition.

nodes.title: Siegel compact dual
nodes.statement: For the genus-g Siegel datum of ShimuraVarieties §P.4 (g≥1) on a symplectic ℚ-space of dimension 2g, μ_h is GSp_{2g}(ℂ)-conjugate to the ℚ-rational cocharacter z↦diag(zI_g,I_g) in a symplectic basis whose first g vectors span a Lagrangian L₀. Its filtration parabolic (D3/filtration-parabolic) is the Siegel parabolic stabilizing a Lagrangian, so the compact dual (D3/compact-dual) is the Lagrangian Grassmannian LG(g,2g), of dimension g(g+1)/2=dim_ℂX. It is already defined over ℚ=E(G,X), and the descended compact dual of D3/reflex-flag-descent has the ℚ-point L₀.
proofSteps: The cocharacter diag(zI_g,I_g) has similitude z and weights 1 on L₀ and 0 on a complementary Lagrangian; it is conjugate to μ_h because both have these weights on a Lagrangian splitting and GSp_{2g}(ℂ) acts transitively on such splittings.
The stabilizer of the filtration L₀⊂V is the Siegel parabolic with Levi GL_g×G_m; G/P is the variety of Lagrangians.
The tangent space at L₀ is the space of symmetric maps L₀→V/L₀, of dimension g(g+1)/2.
The cocharacter is defined over ℚ, so the parabolic type is ℚ-rational and Par_t(G) has the rational point L₀.

sources.match: Milne describes the Siegel datum, its domain of positive or negative complex structures, and computes its reflex field ℚ from a ℚ-rational representative of the μ class; the Lagrangian compact dual is the flag variety of the Siegel parabolic.

hypotheses: The Siegel datum and its reflex field ℚ are ShimuraVarieties §§P.3–P.4's; the filtration parabolic and compact dual are D3/filtration-parabolic and D3/compact-dual.
acceptance: For g=1, LG(1,2)=ℙ¹ and dim=1.
For g=2, LG(2,4) has dimension 3 and is a smooth quadric threefold.
The full Grassmannian Gr(g,2g), of dimension g², is not the compact dual for g≥2.

nodes.title: Scalar-determinant Hilbert datum and its inclusion
nodes.statement: Let G*⊂G=Res_{F/ℚ}GL₂ be the subgroup with determinant in G_m, the group of PELModuli §M5.4's Case C Hilbert datum, whose Shimura datum (G*,X*) is RationalPELDatum.toShimuraDatum of §M0.12. proofSteps: G* is the fibre product of det with the diagonal G_m (D0/hilbert-real-points); the inclusion is a closed immersion.

X* is the G*(ℝ)-class of h. A common determinant t acts on all factors with the same sign, and the determinant-one factors act transitively on each ℍ^±, so X* is the union of the two same-sign products.
G*^der=G^der=Res_{F/ℚ}SL₂ and G*^ad=G^ad=Res_{F/ℚ}PGL₂, so the connected adjoint data agree.
The compact dual of X* is the flag variety of the same parabolic type, hence the same descended Res_{F/ℚ}ℙ¹.

nodes.title: Unipotent Iwahori criterion for neatness
nodes.statement: For a number field F and a compact open K⊂GSp₄(𝔸F,f), choose one rational prime ℓ>5. Suppose every place v|ℓ is absolutely unramified and the projection of K to GSp₄(F_v) is contained in Iw₁(v). Then every k∈K is adelically neat for the faithful ℚ-representation of Res_F/ℚ GSp₄ on the underlying ℚ-space of F⁴, as in Definition 3.2.1. Hence for every g∈GSp₄(𝔸F,f), every γ∈GSp₄(F)∩gKg⁻¹ is rationally neat in that representation. The same certification proves the prime-to-p statement when ℓ≠p and all places above ℓ are retained. For F=ℚ this recovers the one-place criterion. One arbitrary F-place does not suffice for this rational conclusion: see E17.
proofSteps: For each v|ℓ, the shifted degree-four characteristic polynomial and v(ℓ)=1 bound every standard eigenvalue λ by v(λ−1)≥1/4 (D5/local-eigenvalue-bound). Transport through every embedding of F_v into ℚ̄_ℓ; the same normalized bound holds for every eigenvalue of the faithful rational representation, not just one four-dimensional factor.

D5/local-products-bound bounds the whole subgroup generated by these eigenvalues. By AdelicAlgebraicGroups §4.3 (distance of p-adic roots of unity from one), a nontrivial root of unity ζ has v(ζ−1)=0 if its order is prime to ℓ and v(ζ−1)=1/(ℓ^{k−1}(ℓ−1))≤1/(ℓ−1) if it is a primitive ℓ^k-th root; for ℓ>5 both are <1/4. So the ℓ-term of Definition 3.2.1 is torsion free and the global intersection is trivial for every k∈K.

Adelic conjugation preserves each local spectrum. A rational element of a conjugate level has the same eigenvalues in every local realization of its faithful rational representation, so adelic neatness gives rational neatness (AA §4.3's Neat.IsNeatAut). Removing a prime p≠ℓ leaves the certifying term available.

Real z maps to (z,z̄), and conjugation both swaps factors and conjugates coefficients. Supplier coordinate maps retain this convention.

Dual pieces have types (−p,−q); the native dual filtration uses 1−p. The comparison retains the dual representation, not just dimension.
Nm^m corresponds to type (−m,−m), weight −2m. Native Tate twist uses filtration p+m and the tensor comparison identifies the representation twist.
Deligne h(i) acts by i^(q−p), the inverse of the pinned i^(p−q) Weil operator. The inverse-composition conclusion matches Deligne §1.1.2–1.1.4.
